```{r load-clean, eval=TRUE}
# ===== A: data cleaning =====
# Read the untouched download, keep realised stays with valid prices,
# recode categories, drop columns we can't use, and write the cleaned copy.
# Works with our repo layout, or with hotels.csv saved next to this Rmd
# (e.g. the grader's download from our OneDrive folder).
local_copy <- file.exists("hotels.csv")
raw_path <- if (local_copy) "hotels.csv" else "../data/raw/hotels.csv"
clean_path <- if (local_copy) "hotels_clean.csv" else "../data/clean/hotels_clean.csv"
raw <- read_csv(raw_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Step 1: keep realised stays only (cancelled bookings never paid this price).
step1 <- raw %>% filter(is_canceled == 0)

# Step 2: drop 0-night stays and complimentary / invalid prices.
step2 <- step1 %>%
  filter(stays_in_weekend_nights + stays_in_week_nights > 0, adr > 0)

# Step 3: drop rows with undefined or unusable values.
step3 <- step2 %>%
  filter(distribution_channel != "Undefined",  # 1 row, no meaning
         reserved_room_type != "L",            # 4 rows, too rare to estimate
         country != "NULL",                    # guest country unknown
         !is.na(children))

# Step 4: recode, then keep only variables known at booking time.
clean <- step3 %>%
  mutate(
    meal = if_else(meal == "Undefined", "SC", meal),  # both mean "no meal package"
    arrival_date_month = factor(arrival_date_month, levels = month.name),
    domestic = if_else(country == "PRT", "Domestic", "International"),
    is_repeated_guest = factor(is_repeated_guest, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes")),
    across(c(hotel, meal, market_segment, distribution_channel, customer_type,
             reserved_room_type, deposit_type, domestic), factor)
  ) %>%
  select(-is_canceled, -reservation_status, -reservation_status_date,
         -assigned_room_type, -agent, -company, -country,
         -arrival_date_week_number, -arrival_date_day_of_month)

# Rows left after each step (quote these in the Data description).
row_counts <- c(raw = nrow(raw), realised = nrow(step1),
                valid_stay = nrow(step2), final = nrow(clean))

write_csv(clean, clean_path)
```

<!-- ===== A START: Data description (max 300 words; D's table + figure live here too) ===== -->
# Data Description

```{r adr-stats, eval=TRUE}
# Numbers quoted inline in the Data description (A).
fmt <- function(x, d = 0) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ",")
adr <- clean$adr
adr_skew <- mean((adr - mean(adr))^3) / sd(adr)^3

# Predictors planned for the preliminary model (C: build the model from this
# vector so the Data description and the model always agree).
prelim_predictors <- c("lead_time", "hotel", "arrival_date_month",
                       "stays_in_weekend_nights", "stays_in_week_nights",
                       "adults", "children", "meal", "market_segment",
                       "customer_type", "reserved_room_type",
                       "is_repeated_guest", "total_of_special_requests",
                       "domestic")
n_numeric <- sum(sapply(clean[prelim_predictors], is.numeric))
n_categorical <- length(prelim_predictors) - n_numeric
```

*Source and original collection.* We use the Hotel Booking Demand data of @antonio2019, downloaded from TidyTuesday [@tidytuesday]. These are administrative records, not survey data: the authors queried the property-management-system databases of a resort hotel (Algarve) and a city hotel (Lisbon) in Portugal for all bookings due to arrive between July 2015 and August 2017, then removed hotel and customer identifiers. They collected the data to build models predicting booking cancellations.

*Cleaning.* To model prices actually paid, we kept realised stays (`r fmt(row_counts[["realised"]])` of `r fmt(row_counts[["raw"]])`), removed zero-night stays and non-positive rates (`r fmt(row_counts[["valid_stay"]])` left), and dropped rows with an undefined channel, a very rare room type or an unknown country, leaving `r fmt(row_counts[["final"]])` bookings. We cleaned the data in R [@rcore] with the tidyverse [@tidyverse]. The data meet the project requirements: one response and `r length(prelim_predictors)` predictors (`r n_numeric` numerical, `r n_categorical` categorical), summarised in Table 1.

*Response variable.* The average daily rate (ADR), lodging revenue divided by nights stayed [@antonio2019], takes `r fmt(length(unique(adr)))` distinct values, so it is effectively continuous: median `r fmt(median(adr), 2)` (IQR `r fmt(quantile(adr, 0.25))`–`r fmt(quantile(adr, 0.75))`), mean `r fmt(mean(adr), 2)`, SD `r fmt(sd(adr), 2)`, right-skewed (skewness `r fmt(adr_skew, 2)`). Each row is a separate booking, so observations are plausibly independent, though repeat guests and group bookings may share prices; we check this in the residual analysis.

# Preliminary Results

```{r model}
# ===== C: >= 9 predictors + 1 interaction (categorical x another variable) =====
# Tip: reformulate(c(prelim_predictors, "lead_time:hotel"), response = "adr")
# builds the formula from the predictor list in the Data description.
model <- lm(response ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6 + x7 + x8 + x9 + x_cat:x_num,
            data = clean)
```

```{r model-table}
coefs <- broom::tidy(model, conf.int = TRUE)
kable(coefs %>% select(term, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high, p.value),
      digits = 3,
      col.names = c("Term", "Estimate", "SE", "95% CI lower", "95% CI upper", "p-value"),
      caption = "Preliminary model estimates with standard errors and 95% confidence intervals.")
```

```{r conditions, fig.cap="Checking the conditions: (a) response vs fitted values; (b) pairwise scatterplots of the numeric predictors.", fig.height=3.5}
# (a) Condition 1 — conditional mean response: points should scatter around one simple function.
p_cond <- ggplot(tibble(fitted = fitted(model), y = model.response(model.frame(model))),
                 aes(fitted, y)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) + geom_abline(linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Fitted values", y = "Response", title = "(a)")
p_cond
# (b) Condition 2 — conditional mean predictors: no curved relationships between predictors.
# pairs(clean %>% select(where(is.numeric), -response))
```

```{r residual-plots, fig.cap="Residual plots for the preliminary model: (a) residuals vs fitted, (b–…) residuals vs each predictor, (last) normal QQ plot.", fig.height=6}
res_df <- tibble(fitted = fitted(model), resid = resid(model)) %>%
  bind_cols(model.frame(model) %>% select(-1))

p_rf <- ggplot(res_df, aes(fitted, resid)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Fitted values", y = "Residuals", title = "(a)")

# One residual-vs-predictor plot per predictor (boxplots for categorical ones).
pred_names <- setdiff(names(res_df), c("fitted", "resid"))
p_preds <- map(pred_names, function(v) {
  g <- ggplot(res_df, aes(.data[[v]], resid)) + labs(x = v, y = "Residuals")
  if (is.numeric(res_df[[v]])) g + geom_point(alpha = 0.3) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed")
  else g + geom_boxplot()
})

p_qq <- ggplot(res_df, aes(sample = resid)) + stat_qq(alpha = 0.3) + stat_qq_line() +
  labs(x = "Theoretical quantiles", y = "Sample quantiles", title = "Normal QQ")

wrap_plots(c(list(p_rf), p_preds, list(p_qq)), ncol = 3)
```
